.@bhorowitz on the $10 album that was worth $5 million to his career, and what @Nas said when he tried to pay it back:

"Paid in Full is an organization meant to honor the legacy of the people who created one of the most important musical art forms of all time, hip-hop, and make sure that they're paid in full financially, spiritually, and culturally."

"It always bothered me that I bought Paid in Full, the album, for $10, and people in tech know this, I probably got at least $5 million worth of value out of that record. But there was no way to pay it back. And it needed to be paid back."

"Steve Stoute said, 'It's not only a good idea, but it's a very timely idea, 'cause people are talking about this right now, but they're not doing anything.'"

"People are saying, 'Oh, these rappers, these old guys, they don't have any money. They're dusty.' And these are very, very important guys. But nobody's doing anything. And so I thought, well, let's do something."

"Quincy Jones had a thing called the Jazz Foundation, where he would get money to the old jazz guys. I told it to Nas, and Nas said, 'That's not gonna work that way in hip-hop, because in hip-hop you can't just give somebody money. It has to be more than that. It has to be a recognition of what they did and who they are.'"

"And so that's when we got the idea of, well, let's have a big awards show, have this idea of the Grandmaster Award for the true greats of hip-hop, and then invite everybody to honor these guys."

@bhorowitz @Nas @SteveStoute

quoted_tweet.text:
Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg with Nas, Steve Stoute, and Grandmaster Caz on the Paid in Full Foundation

Caz penned rhymes that became Rapper's Delight. Even with his name in them, he got nothing.

The Paid in Full foundation honors the people who created hip-hop by making sure they're "paid in full," financially, spiritually, and culturally.

As Nas points out, money alone reads as a handout. So the grant comes attached to the honor. Each year at the foundation's Hip Hop Grandmaster Awards, pioneers are celebrated by the artists they inspired.

Caz ultimately received a five-year grant, bought a house, and left the projects. In his words: "The thing is the honor. The thing is putting you in the light that you deserve to be in."

Ben says he bought Paid in Full (the album) for $10 and got at least $5 million worth of value out of the record, with no way to pay it back.

The vision is paying the debt. Felicia Horowitz runs the foundation. She and Ben are matching donations 2.5 to 1, and every dollar goes to the artists.

http://paidinfullfoundation.org

text:
.@bhorowitz and @SteveStoute on the original sin of hip-hop, and @GrandmasterCaz on how the Paid in Full Foundation changed his life:

"It's the original sin of hip-hop... Not enough people knew, but the right people knew. The industry knew."

"Caz wrote the rhyme that became Rapper's Delight. Those were his rhymes. With his name in the rhymes."

"The first hip-hop hit was stolen from him, and he didn't get what he deserved. And everybody knew it, but no one ever did anything about it, never said anything about it."

Caz: "When Paid in Full called me, it was like, now this is gonna change your life. I bought a house. I moved out the projects."

"I've lived in the Bronx all my life... The last thoughts in my head for the last, like, 10, 15 years, I don't wanna die in the projects. I don't wanna end here. And it didn't. And it's not."

"My life has improved drastically. I got a comfort. I got like a cushion that I never had. Everything was day to day. Everything was run out, grind, hustle... because I have to."

"Hip-hop don't have Social Security. Hip-hop don't have no health benefits or none of that. You have to work. You gotta stay out there."

" We were talking about some people didn't know if it was a scam or whatever. A couple people thought it was like a handout, 'Yo, I don't need this. I'm good.' Nah, it's not about that... The thing is the honor. The thing is putting you in the light that you deserve to be in."

@GrandmasterCaz @SteveStoute @Nas @bhorowitz
